analysis.reason: The paper provides an improved theoretical framework combining two-body diffusion and collisionless chaotic diving orbits in flattened galactic potentials, yielding a key boost factor $1 + \ln(j_d/j_t)$ to tidal disruption event (TDE) rates.
analysis.result: Disruption rates in flattened potentials are enhanced over the classical loss-cone rate $\Gamma_{\rm cl}$ by a multiplicative factor $\Gamma / \Gamma_{\rm cl} \approx 1 + \ln(j_d / j_t)$, typically yielding an order-of-magnitude increase ($\sim 10\times$) for characteristic chaotic diving thresholds $j_d \gtrsim 0.1$. When diffusion is weak ($\sigma \lesssim 0.1 j_t$), disruptions are highly anisotropic and aligned near the disk plane ($|\cos i| \to 1$), while in the well-mixed regime ($\sigma \gtrsim j_t$), the penetration factor distribution follows $p(\beta) \propto \beta^{-2}$.
analysis.problem: Classical loss-cone theory based solely on two-body relaxation underestimates disruption rates by omitting chaotic orbit migration, whereas previous collisionless chaotic models neglected depletion of the diving region and diffusion coupling, hindering self-consistent equilibrium predictions.
analysis.method: The authors construct a 2D equilibrium Fokker-Planck model $p(j_z, j)$ coupling two-body scattering, rapid uniform chaotic redistribution within diving orbits ($j < j_d$), and pericenter loss ($j < j_t$), supplemented by 1D/2D analytical Bessel solutions and walker-based Monte Carlo simulations.
citation_leads: 2 The loss cone and the loss wedge: “Thus any system with $j_{z}<j_{t}$ and $j<j_{d}$ has a chance of disruption from chaotic angular momentum redistribution alone.”
4.1 Total rate and separability: “We seek a fixed-point solution: a distribution $p(j_{z},j)$ that is unchanged after one full cycle of scattering, diving, loss, and renormalisation.”
5.4.2 Comparing to $Gammacl$: “Another benchmark to compare to is how much the inclusion of the diving region boosts the rate of disruptions compared to the classical case.”

6 Discussion and Conclusions: “We present analytical arguments and toy models that estimate the boost to disruption rates, $\Gamma$, compared to the classical case which ignores diving orbits, $\Gamma_{cl}$, of approximately $\Gamma/\Gamma_{cl}\sim 1+\ln(j_{d}/j_{t})”
analysis.research_progress: Establishes a unified analytical and numerical loss-cone formalism that self-consistently couples two-body scattering with chaotic phase-space mixing, proving the robust scaling $\Gamma / \Gamma_{\rm cl} \approx 1 + \ln(j_d / j_t)$ and determining the resulting orientation and penetration distributions.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates whether low-mass binary black hole events like GW241011 and GW241110 are naturally expected within hierarchical merger channels and formulates likelihood-ratio classification metrics across spin-precession parameter space.
analysis.result: Hierarchical mergers (1G+2G) are classified via likelihood ratio metrics: in simulated realistic cluster (CMC) mergers, the $\chi_{\mathrm{p}}$ metric alone achieves a $24\%$ ($182$ events) classification rate, whereas a joint $(\chi_{\mathrm{eff}}, \chi_{\mathrm{p}})$ metric increases identification to $35\%$ ($265$ events) by eliminating face-on selection vulnerability. Binary mass ratio $q$ is identified as the dominant intrinsic driver of identification over primary mass $m_{1,\mathrm{det}}$, with unequal-mass binaries ($q \lesssim 0.4$) dramatically improving precession measurement precision.

analysis.reason: The study directly constrains the delay-time distribution (DTD) of binary neutron star mergers, showing an unexpected preference for multi-Gyr delay times that challenges standard isolated binary evolution models and impacts kilonova and short gamma-ray burst progenitor rates.
analysis.result: The stellar population analysis of NGC 4993 yields a mass-weighted age of $12.4^{+0.5}_{-0.7}\,\mathrm{Gyr}$. Under an efficiency-normalized power-law DTD model ($\mathrm{DTD} = A t^{\alpha}$), the minimum delay time is constrained to $t_{\rm min} > 7.5\pm 0.2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ (90% credible level) and $t_{\rm min} > 5.6\pm 0.2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ (95% credible level), peaking at $12.6\pm 0.7\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ for $\alpha = -1$. The empirical $(12.6\,\mathrm{Gyr}, -1)$ model is favored over the canonical $(10\,\mathrm{Myr}, -1)$ model by a Bayes/likelihood factor of 41–138.
analysis.reading_entry: III.2 Constraints on the Minimum Delay Time and Power-Law Index
analysis.problem: Standard binary neutron star evolution predicts a delay-time distribution $dN/dt \propto t^{-1}$ with $t_{\rm min} \sim 10\,\mathrm{Myr}$, implying that short-delay mergers should outnumber long-delay mergers by $\sim 16:1$, creating a severe statistical tension with GW170817 originating in an extremely old stellar population.
analysis.method: The host galaxy NGC 4993 was analyzed using prospector and FSPS with MIST isochrones and MILES spectral libraries across 14 photometric bands and VLT/MUSE integral field spectroscopy to reconstruct its non-parametric star formation history (SFH). Poisson likelihood frameworks incorporating cosmic star formation history $\psi(t)$ and DTD parameterizations ($A t^\alpha$) were evaluated via nested sampling with dynesty.

analysis.reason: This work develops the ARISE framework linking binary black hole (BBH) mergers in AGN disks to cosmological AGN and SMBH growth, providing testable merger rates and population predictions for current LVK observations and next-generation gravitational wave detectors like the Einstein Telescope.
analysis.result: The local comoving merger rate density is primarily governed by the disk viscosity parameter $\alpha$: at $z=0.2$, $\mathcal{R}(z=0.2)=24^{+13}_{-8}\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ for $\alpha=0.01$ (peaking at $z\simeq 1.8$ at $280^{+170}_{-110}\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$), whereas $\alpha=0.1$ reduces the rates by roughly an order of magnitude to $0.5\text{--}6\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ ($f_{\mathrm{AGN}}\sim 2\%\text{--}38\%$), making $\alpha=0.1$ consistent with empirical electromagnetic flare upper limits ($f_{\mathrm{AGN}}\lesssim 40\%$). For the Einstein Telescope ($T_{\mathrm{obs}}=1\,\mathrm{yr}$, SNR $\rho>12$), expected detections reach $0.9\text{--}1.6\times 10^5$ events for $\alpha=0.01$ and $\sim 10^4$ for $\alpha=0.1$, with super-Eddington models (CAT-SE) predicting persistent detections out to $z\simeq 8$.
analysis.problem: Current ground-based gravitational wave detectors only observe stellar-mass BBH mergers out to $z\sim 1.5$, leaving the high-redshift ($z\gtrsim 2\text{--}10$) evolution of BBH merger rates, their connection to SMBH accretion pathways (Eddington-limited vs. super-Eddington), and the fraction of LVK mergers produced in AGN disks unconstrained.
analysis.method: The ARISE framework couples a semi-analytic AGN disk dynamical model (FastClusterAGN accounting for Type I/II migration, gas damping, pairing with semi-major axis distribution $p(a)\propto a^{9/2}$, and gravitational wave hardening) with cosmological semi-analytic models of SMBH growth (CAT-EL and CAT-SE). Source-frame merger rate densities $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{AGN}}(z)$ are computed by integrating the mean galaxy merger rate $\bar{\Gamma}$ weighted by the comoving active AGN number density $n_{\mathrm{AGN}}(z)$ and active fraction $f_{\mathrm{active}}(M_\bullet, z)=\frac{\int_{\dot{M}_{\bullet,\mathrm{min}}}^\infty d\dot{M}_\bullet\,\Phi}{\int_0^\infty d\dot{M}_\bullet\,\Phi}$.
assumptions: Hierarchical BH growth terminates only if the cumulative merger timescale exceeds the disk lifetime $\tau$, a recoil kick ejects the remnant, or local BH seeds are exhausted.
limits: Disk physics neglects complex 3D magnetohydrodynamic turbulence and disk-wind mass loss, relying on 1D Sirko & Goodman thin-disk solutions and steady-state migration regimes.

analysis.reason: The paper studies accretion-regulated AGN jet feedback and propagation in turbulent multiphase ISM using Arepo simulations, establishing scaling relations between jet power, turbulence Mach number, and efficiency factor, which is physically relevant to relativistic jet propagation and compact radio environments (FR0s).
analysis.result: Turbulence plays a dual role by driving gas into the central accretion region and providing low-density channels for outward jet breakout. Without turbulence ($\mathfrak{M}=0$), self-limiting accretion confines jet power to $\le 10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ (dropping to $<10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$), whereas supersonic turbulence ($\mathfrak{M}=4$) sustains median jet powers of $10^{40}\text{--}10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, reproducing FR0-like Eddington ratios $L_{\rm jet}/L_{\rm Edd}$. For low efficiencies $\varepsilon$, jet power scales linearly with $\varepsilon$, while exceeding $\varepsilon > 10^{-1}$ leads to strong self-limiting accretion by expelling central gas reservoirs.
analysis.reading_entry: III.3 Dependence on the ISM Mach number
analysis.problem: How interstellar medium (ISM) turbulence regulates both the fueling of supermassive black hole accretion and the confinement or breakout of self-consistently launched AGN jets, resolving the severe shut-off of cold accretion observed in quiescent/uniform media.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the theoretical hydrodynamics of advection-dominated accretion flows (ADAF) around black holes in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld (EiBI) modified gravity, which lacks direct application to high-energy transients, FRBs, supernovae engines, or relativistic jets.
analysis.result: In the $s=-1$ branch of EiBI gravity, the ADAF-like flow exhibits systematically lower radial velocity $v_{r}$, sound speed $c_{s}$, specific angular momentum $l$, and temperature $T$, alongside higher density $\rho$ and disk scale height $H$ compared to standard Paczyński-Wiita (PW) gravity. The sonic point shifts inward from $r_{\rm sp} \simeq 3.7673\,r_{s}$ to $3.6072\,r_{s}$. Furthermore, the normalized mass accretion rate $\dot{M}/\dot{M}_{\rm B}$ varies from $\simeq 0.054$ to $\simeq 0.058$ as the core radius $r_{c}$ increases, but decreases from $\simeq 0.054$ to $\simeq 0.045$ as the charge parameter $r_{q}$ increases.
analysis.problem: Evaluating how deviations from General Relativity in the strong-field regime, specifically under Palatini Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld gravity, modify the hydrodynamic and thermodynamic structure of low-angular-momentum transonic accretion flows onto black holes.
analysis.method: Constructed an effective Paczyński-Wiita-like pseudo-Newtonian potential $\Phi_{\rm PW}(r) = -\left(1+\frac{s r_{c}^{4}}{x(r)^{4}}\right)\left(\frac{r_{s}x(r)-r_{q}^{2}}{-r_{s}x(r)+x(r)^{2}+r_{q}^{2}}+1\right)$ mapped from static spherically symmetric black hole solutions in EiBI gravity, coupled with stationary, axisymmetric ADAF hydrodynamic equations with Shakura-Sunyaev viscosity $\nu = \alpha c_{s}^{2}/\Omega_{K}$, solved as a two-point boundary value problem using a relaxation method.
citation_leads: Effects of Eddington-inspired Born–Infeld Gravity on Black Hole Accretion: “Black holes offer a unique setting to test gravity in the strong-field regime, where deviations from General Relativity are expected to be most pronounced.”
II.3 PW-like potential: “The pseudo-Newtonian potential is chosen so that the extrema of the Newtonian effective potential coincide with those for timelike geodesics of the spacetime.”

IV Results: “Compared with the standard PW case, the EiBI gravity solution predicts lower $v_{r}$, $c_{s}$, $l$, and $T$ over most of the accretion flow. In contrast, $\rho$ and $H$ increase systematically.”
analysis.research_progress: Extends ADAF-like accretion flow dynamics from standard GR/Paczyński-Wiita frameworks to Ricci-Based Gravities (RBGs), establishing that black hole charge $r_{q}$ exerts a more pronounced suppression on $\dot{M}/\dot{M}_{\rm B}$ than the core radius $r_{c}$.

Filled circles denote the sonic points. Sonic point is $r_{sp}=3.7673\,r_{s}$ for standard ADAF -like, and is $r_{sp}=3.6072\,r_{s}$. For Palatini gravity $s=-1$, $r_{c}=10^{-32}\,r_{s}$; $r_{q}=10^{-30}\,r_{s}$. These values are motivated by the constraints on the electric charge in [ 54 ].

analysis.reason: This work quantitatively establishes how static shear strains exponentially accelerate self-diffusion in Yukawa crystals via Frenkel pair nucleation, providing key microphysical inputs for magnetar crustal creep, stress relaxation, and burst trigger mechanics.
analysis.result: Static shear strain $\varepsilon$ exponentially enhances self-diffusion by lowering the activation energy barrier for Frenkel defect pair formation via the stored elastic strain energy $\sigma = \frac{1}{2}\mu\varepsilon^2$ within an activation volume $V^*$ containing $N_{\rm act} \equiv n_i V^* \approx 31 \pm 1$ ions across astrophysically relevant screenings ($\kappa \lesssim 1$). The modified diffusion coefficient follows $D(\Gamma^*,\varepsilon) = D_0(\Gamma^*) \exp\left[\frac{1}{2} N_{\rm act} \tilde{\mu} \Gamma \varepsilon^2\right]$, which scales near melting as $D(\Gamma^*,\varepsilon) = \frac{787}{\Gamma^*} \exp\left[-\left(20 - 5\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{0.1}\right)^2\right)\Gamma^*\right]$, increasing diffusion by orders of magnitude at high coupling $\Gamma^*$.
analysis.problem: Understanding whether and how static elastic shear stress alters self-diffusion in body-centered cubic (bcc) Yukawa crystals relevant to neutron star crusts and white dwarf interiors, specifically differentiating whether strain modifies defect migration mobility or defect pair nucleation rates.
analysis.method: Performed classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of bcc Yukawa crystals with frozen boundary layers under static $xy$-shear strain using LAMMPS, tracking ion mean-squared displacements (MSDs) across various coupling parameters $\Gamma^*$ and screening parameters $\kappa$ to extract defect nucleation rates $\nu(\varepsilon)$ and activation volumes $V^*$.
citation_leads: Stress-enhanced diffusion in Yukawa crystals: “We simulate sheared Yukawa crystals and show that a static elastic strain exponentially enhances diffusion due to the additional elastic energy stored in the region that participates in Frenkel pair formation relative to the unstrained”
IV Results: “This is perhaps the most useful key result of this work, namely, that $N_{\rm act}\approx 31\pm 1$ holds across astrophysically relevant screenings.”

V Discussion: “In magnetars, magnetic stresses drive the crust toward failure; stress-enhanced diffusion in the most strained regions opens a channel for thermally activated creep and gradual stress relaxation”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that strain acts exclusively on the Arrhenius defect nucleation rate $\ln[\nu(\varepsilon)/\nu_0] = \frac{1}{2} N_{\rm act} \tilde{\mu} \Gamma \varepsilon^2$ rather than defect hopping speed, confirming a universal activation particle number $N_{\rm act} \approx 31$ that corresponds to the first two neighbor shells of the bcc lattice.

figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: The mean squared displacement increases with shear strain at fixed $\Gamma^{*}$, showing strain-enhanced diffusion in the simulated Yukawa crystal.

analysis.reason: The paper identifies $^{250}\mathrm{Cm}$ as the primary gamma-ray emitter in strong $r$-process remnants at ages of $2{,}000 - 20{,}000\ \mathrm{yr}$, providing crucial diagnostic line predictions for high-energy remnant observations.
analysis.result: In strong $r$-process ejecta, $^{250}\mathrm{Cm}$ achieves a mass fraction $\gtrapprox 0.2\%$ (up to $2.0\%$) and dominates the $0.2 - 5\ \mathrm{MeV}$ $\gamma$-ray photon budget at $t \sim 2{,}000 - 20{,}000\ \mathrm{yr}$ with peak emission fractions of $67\% - 87\%$. With a total half-life $\tau_{1/2} \approx 8300\ \mathrm{yr}$ governed by spontaneous fission, $\alpha$-, and $\beta^-$-decay, the incident energy line flux scales as $F_{\gamma}(t) = \frac{M_{\mathrm{Cm}} E_{\gamma} R_{\gamma}(t)}{4\pi D^2}$, yielding prominent diagnostic lines including $^{250}\mathrm{Bk}$ ($989, 1032\ \mathrm{keV}$), $^{246\mathrm{m}}\mathrm{Am}$ ($1079\ \mathrm{keV}$), and fission product $^{140}\mathrm{La}$ ($1596\ \mathrm{keV}$).
analysis.problem: Identifying unambiguous, long-lived electromagnetic signatures of heavy actinide nucleosynthesis in aging supernova or neutron star merger remnants to confirm the occurrence of a strong $r$-process.
analysis.method: Performed $15{,}625$ nucleosynthesis simulations using the PRISM reaction network across parameter space ($\rho_0 \in [10^6, 10^{9.5}]\ \mathrm{g\ cm^{-3}}$, $\tau \in [10^{-3.6}, 10^{-1}]\ \mathrm{s}$, $Y_e \in [0.005, 0.5]$), combined with the GEF fission code and late-time secular equilibrium gamma-ray spectral modeling $S^\gamma(E, t) = \sum F(t) S^\gamma(E)$.

analysis.reason: The paper directly addresses prompt coherent radio counterpart searches (FRB-like emission) from compact binary coalescences using gravitational-wave early warnings, combining RL-based telescope pointing optimization with DSA and the Chronoscope backend.
analysis.problem: Optimizing slewing and pointing schedules for single-pointing array telescopes (DSA) under rapidly evolving, uncertain gravitational-wave early-warning localization maps to capture millisecond-duration prompt coherent radio bursts around compact binary coalescences.
analysis.method: Formulated a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process from $t=-60\,\mathrm{s}$ to $+20\,\mathrm{s}$ discretized at $\Delta t = 1\,\mathrm{s}$ using PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) on simulated O5 HLV early-warning localization sequences (BAYESTAR at 29, 38, 56, and 1024 Hz), gated by a classifier/regression model dispatch, and validated trajectory tracking on prototype DSA antennas at OVRO with azimuth slew rates up to $3.8^\circ\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.
assumptions: Array dishes share a single unified pointing trajectory with a circular top-hat effective field of view of $\sim 18\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ and elevation cutoff $\ge 20^\circ$.
limits: Evaluated primarily on Gaussian noise and idealized BAYESTAR localization maps rather than non-Gaussian, non-stationary real detector glitches.
Geometric immediate observability is limited to $37\%$ of all isotropic merger events due to elevation and horizon cuts.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “propagation delay relative to infinite frequency is approximately $0.4$–$4$ s at 1 GHz. Exploiting this window requires sufficiently rapid alerts and telescope response,”
II.2 Environment and observability constraints: “We model the telescope as a finite-field-of-view (FoV), fast-slewing instrument with realistic observability constraints.”

II.5 Follow-up reachability for the simulated population: “At a random merger time, $37\%$ of the simulated events are above the adopted $20^{\circ}$ minimum elevation and are therefore immediately observable.”

V Summary: “With the planned Chronoscope beamformed backend, optimized DSA follow-up can reach fluence limits of $\sim$20 mJy ms, probing millisecond bursts with isotropic-equivalent energies of $10^{35}$–$10^{36}$ erg and luminosities of”

A.7 Gaussian-noise localization sequences: “Under measurement noise, the dispatch stage requires one modification: a regression model that predicts the expected RL-minus-baseline reward difference from the same five early-map features replaces the binary classifier”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that RL-guided sequential pointing, gated by early map morphometrics, boosts post-merger probability capture over peak-tracking baselines by $3.15\%$ on complex posterior distributions, and verified that planned DSA/Chronoscope follow-up can constrain pre-merger magnetospheric flaring ($L_{\rm EM} \sim 10^{44}\text{--}10^{45}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$) and hypermassive neutron star collapse bursts.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Example paired rollouts comparing the RL policy with the visibility-aware peak-tracking baseline. In each row, the left panel shows the earliest BAYESTAR map (logarithmic stretch) with the $90\%$ credible contours of all four localization stages, the dashed curve marks the $20^{\circ}$ minimum-elevation boundary, with the inaccessible sky below it shaded. The pointing trajectories of the two controllers are colored by episode time, and the right panel zooms in on the final localization. Top row: an arc-like localization in which both controllers reach the dominant mode, and the RL trajectory remains slightly better aligned with the broader posterior structure, yielding a capture reward a few percent above the baseline. Bottom row: an event whose pre-merger posterior maxima are noticeably offset from the eventual source position; the peak-tracking controller follows these offset maxima and is still approaching the source at merger, while the learned policy settles onto it earlier and accumulates roughly $40\%$ more capture reward, mostly in the heavily weighted post-merger window.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: The paired sky-localization and pointing trajectories show how evolving, sometimes offset GW posterior maxima affect the radio telescope's ability to reach the source before merger. In the lower example, the learned policy reaches the source earlier than peak tracking and earns roughly 40% more capture reward, mainly in the post-merger window.

figures.caption: Figure 3: GW170817-like localization evolution for a two-detector Hanford–Livingston network with Virgo removed (top block) and a three-detector Hanford–Livingston–Virgo network (bottom block), for the same injection and localization pipeline. Panels show the BAYESTAR sky maps at the 29, 38, 56, and 1024 Hz frequency cutoffs. The star marks the true source position and the dot the posterior maximum. With three detectors the maximum coincides with the true position from the earliest map, whereas the two-detector posterior is an extended arc whose maximum lies tens of degrees from the source until shortly before merger.

analysis.result:
GRB 241113B is confirmed as an intrinsically soft Type II GRB (XRR/XRF) observed on-axis within a redshift range $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 3.5$. Joint prompt spectral fitting favors a cutoff power-law (CPL) model with photon index $\alpha = -1.80^{+0.16}_{-0.10}$ and $E^{\mathrm{obs}}_{\mathrm{peak}} \approx 35	ext{--}37	ext{ keV}$. The prompt duration follows an energy-dependent scaling law $\log T_{90} = \alpha \log(E/50\,\mathrm{keV}) + \log K_{50}$ with $\alpha = -0.35^{+0.10}_{-0.06}$ ($K_{50} = 54.2^{+2.8}_{-4.2}$). The early multiband afterglow peaks at deceleration time $t_b = 263^{+68}_{-91}\,\mathrm{s}$ and decays with $\alpha_2 = -1.40^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$ and spectral index $ eta_{\mathrm{OX}} = 0.66^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$. VegasAfterglow modeling confirms a relativistic top-hat jet propagating into a wind-like circumstellar medium ($s=2$) in the slow cooling regime ($
u_m < 
u_{\mathrm{opt}} < 
u_{\mathrm{X}} < 
u_c$) with electron index $p = 2.31 \pm 0.08$. The bulk Lorentz factor is constrained to $\Gamma_0 > 100$ (posterior bounds $\Gamma_0 \sim 125	ext{--}263$), ruling out both shock breakout (SBO) and high baryon loading (dirty fireball) scenarios.
analysis.problem: Unveiling the physical origin of prompt spectral softness in X-ray rich bursts (XRR) and X-ray flashes (XRF): whether they are driven by geometric viewing angle effects (off-axis jets), relativistic shock breakouts, dirty fireballs with heavy baryon loading ($\Gamma_0 \ll 100$), or intrinsic jet dissipative processes.
analysis.method: Joint prompt spectral fitting across 0.5–1000 keV combining EP/WXT, SVOM/ECLAIRs, and SVOM/GRM with PL, CPL, and Band models. analysis.result: Dynamic radial stability is strictly governed by the fundamental mode frequency $\omega_0^2 > 0$. Strong repulsive self-interaction ($y=10^3$) yields a stiffer dark matter equation of state that supports extended dark halos around compact ordinary matter cores, with maximum stable masses scaling as $M_{\rm max} \propto m_f^{-2}$, reaching up to $66.79 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 2\ \mathrm{GeV}$, $10.69 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 5\ \mathrm{GeV}$, and $2.672 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 10\ \mathrm{GeV}$. The gravitational redshift at the visible ordinary matter surface is given by $1+z_{\mathrm{OM}} = e^{\Delta\Phi_{\rm halo}}/\sqrt{1-2M/R}$ where $\Delta\Phi_{\rm halo} = \int_{R_{\mathrm{OM}}}^{R}[m(r)+4\pi r^{3}p(r)]/[r(r-2m(r))]\,\mathrm{d}r$, allowing stable configurations to exceed the standard vacuum Buchdahl redshift limit ($z=2$).

analysis.reason: It addresses the rapid identification and ranking of kilonova counterparts to gravitational-wave (GW) triggers in large-scale optical surveys like Vera C. Rubin/LSST, directly serving compact object multimessenger follow-up.
analysis.result: In candidate galleries containing 5000 transients, MAGIKS achieves a Recall@1 of $39.8\%$ (compared to $4.8\%$ for optical-only and $0.2\%$ for sky-localization-only baselines) and an MRR of $0.488$; for GW170817 under Rubin observing conditions, Recall@1 reaches $87.3\%$ and Recall@10 reaches $95.7\%$, while pairwise binary classification yields an AUROC of $0.983$ and an accuracy of $0.942$.
analysis.problem: Wide-field optical searches following GW triggers (BNS and NSBH mergers) are heavily contaminated by thousands of spatio-temporally compatible non-kilonova transients (e.g., SNe, AGNs, TDEs), where pure optical classification or spatial sky-map priors alone fail to jointly assess physical consistency.
analysis.method: An align-before-fuse multimodal architecture that combines a GW encoder (MLP for 7 scalar parameters including $\mathcal{M}_c^{\rm det}$, spins, $\cos\iota$, and $d_L$, plus a 1D-CNN for 3D sky maps) and an optical encoder (modified mTAN with SNR-biased attention for irregular multiband light curves), pre-aligned via time-aware contrastive loss and fused via dual cross-attention conditioned on physical ejecta properties $\bm{\psi} = (\log_{10}(M_{\rm dyn}/M_\odot), \log_{10}(M_{\rm wind}/M_\odot), |\cos\iota|, \log_{10}(d_L/\mathrm{Gpc}))$.
citation_leads: MAGIKS: Multimodal Alignment and Gravitational-Wave-Conditioned Interaction for Kilonova Search: “In the largest evaluated galleries, each containing 5000 candidates, MAGIKS ranks the true counterpart first for 39.8% of queries, compared with 4.8% for optical-only ranking and 0.2% for sky-localization-only ranking.”
IV.2 Retrieval ablations: “In the variant without cross-attention, the cross-attention fusion mechanism is replaced by concatenating the encoder feature vectors before the classification head.”

IV.4 Classification ablation experiments: “MAGIKS provides the strongest overall classification performance, with AUROC of 0.983, AUPRC of 0.951, accuracy of 0.942, precision of 0.877, and $F_{1}$ of 0.885.”

IV.5 Sensitivity to individual GW parameters: “We construct a physics-informed empirical bridge as a data-driven reference for the physical associations accessible to MAGIKS. Without using a deep-learning model, the bridge maps the GW query and the optical light curve independently”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that conditioning optical counterpart ranking on GW scalar posteriors and sky maps simultaneously improves candidate retrieval efficiency by nearly an order of magnitude over optical-only classifiers in dense contaminant fields ($N = 5000$).

figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the proposed multimodal framework for gravitational-wave-triggered kilonova counterpart search. The upper stream encodes the gravitational-wave trigger using source-parameter descriptors and the sky-localization map: scalar parameters are projected with a multilayer perceptron (MLP), while the skymap is processed by a one-dimensional convolutional network and pooled into a localization feature. The lower stream encodes Rubin/LSST optical alerts using irregularly sampled multiband light curves and sky coordinates: temporal samples are represented on a reference time grid with time embeddings and encoded by the Multi-Time Attention Network (mTAN) module, while coordinates are encoded separately. The contrastive-learning branch projects the gravitational-wave and optical representations into a shared embedding space and uses a supervised contrastive objective with a time-compatibility term to favour physically plausible pairs. The fusion branch performs two explicit cross-modal matching operations, comparing optical coordinates with the gravitational-wave localization and gravitational-wave source descriptors with the optical temporal evolution, and produces the final ranking score for counterpart retrieval.
figures.label: Fig. 1

analysis.reason: This work explores how a first-order quark-hadron phase transition (PT) in core-collapse supernovae naturally generates the observed high-mass peak ($1.55\text{--}1.72\,M_\odot$) of neutron stars through accretion delay before the second collapse.
analysis.result: The phase transition triggers a second collapse and shock wave, with the delay time $\Delta t_{\mathrm{collapse}}$ anti-correlating with progenitor compactness $\xi_{1.75}$. Lower-compactness progenitors accrete longer before reaching the PT onset density, leaving heavier remnants and naturally concentrating neutron star gravitational masses into narrow high-mass peaks at $\sim 1.70\,M_\odot$ (RDF1.1, ranging $1.66\text{--}1.72\,M_\odot$) or $1.55\text{--}1.70\,M_\odot$ (RDF1.2). The critical compactness dividing explosion from black hole formation is $\xi_{1.75} \sim 0.59\text{--}0.69$ for RDF1.1 and $\sim 1.04\text{--}1.07$ for RDF1.2.
analysis.reading_entry: III. RESULTS - C. PT induced mass clustering and the higher mass peak
analysis.problem: Observed neutron star mass distributions show a bimodal structure with a high-mass peak around $1.75\text{--}1.8\,M_\odot$, which standard neutrino-driven core-collapse supernova simulations typically fail to reproduce because high-compactness progenitors usually collapse directly into black holes rather than exploding.
analysis.method: Performed systematic 1D general-relativistic hydrodynamic simulations using the `GR1D` code with M1 neutrino transport across solar-metallicity progenitors ($13\text{--}120\,M_\odot$, with step $\Delta M = 0.2\,M_\odot$ for $13\text{--}30\,M_\odot$). Used hybrid equations of state (RDF1.1 and RDF1.2) combining DD2 with a relativistic density functional quark model with onset thresholds $\rho_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 4.07 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ ($M_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 1.60\,M_\odot$) and $\rho_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 3.15 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ ($M_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 1.44\,M_\odot$). Compactness was defined via $\xi_M = \frac{M / M_\odot}{R(M_{\mathrm{bary}} = M) / (1000\,\mathrm{km})}$.

analysis.reason: The study demonstrates that structured jets substantially enhance off-axis very-high-energy (VHE) external inverse-Compton (EIC) emission from short GRBs compared to top-hat jets, offering critical multi-messenger detection prospects for CTAO and gravitational wave follow-ups.
analysis.result: Structured jets (Gaussian and power-law) yield much stronger off-axis $1\,\mathrm{TeV}$ EIC emission than top-hat jets due to relativistic beaming and lateral energy profiles. In the coasting phase with constant seed photon luminosity, the EIC flux scales as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm EIC} \propto T$ in the Thomson regime for $\varepsilon_m^{\rm EIC} < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_c^{\rm EIC}$, and rapidly decays as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm EIC} \propto T^{-33/7}$ at $T \gtrsim T_a \sim 300\,\mathrm{s}$, whereas synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) emission rises sharply as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm SSC} \propto T^4$ before dominating after the deceleration stage ($T \sim 5 \times 10^3\,\mathrm{s}$).
analysis.problem: Whether off-axis short GRBs can produce detectable VHE gamma rays via EIC scattering of extended emission, X-ray plateau, or kilonova seed photons within realistic structured jet geometries.
analysis.method: Numerical modeling using the AMES code integrating emissions over equal-arrival-time surfaces, incorporating Klein-Nishina suppression, forward shock relativistic electron dynamics, and external seed photon fields characterized by broken power-law spectra ($G(\varepsilon)$ with break $\varepsilon_b = E_b / \Gamma$, $\beta_1 = 0.5$, $\beta_2 = 2.0$) and temporal luminosity decay $L(T) \propto T^{-\alpha}$.
citation_leads: Enhanced Detectability of Very-High-Energy Gamma Rays from Off-Axis Short Gamma-Ray Bursts: Impacts of Structured Jets and External Inverse-Compton Scattering: “These X-ray photons can serve as seed photons for external inverse-Compton (EIC) scattering by relativistic electrons in the jet, producing very-high-energy (VHE) gamma rays.”
III.1 Comparison of Jet Structures: “In contrast, the EIC emission from the top-hat jet is strongly suppressed for off-axis observers because of relativistic beaming effect.”

analysis.result: SN 2025dys reached a peak bolometric luminosity of $L = (8.57\pm 0.41)\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with early X-ray emission detected at $L_{\rm X} \approx 7.55\times 10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Modeling with CSI and radioactive decay requires an ejecta mass $M_{\rm ej} \approx 2.45\text{--}2.69\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, kinetic energy $E_{\rm K} \approx 0.37\text{--}0.46\,\mathrm{foe}$, circumstellar medium mass $M_{\rm CSM} \approx 0.54\text{--}0.76\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, and an optical depth of $\tau_{\rm CSM} = 13$ from early electron-scattering wings.
analysis.problem: Unraveling whether the high peak luminosity and spectral evolution of the peculiar transient SN 2025dys are driven by radioactive decay, a central magnetar engine, or shock interaction with a confined, dense circumstellar medium around a stripped-envelope progenitor.
analysis.method: Multi-band photometry fitting via MOSFiT testing pure radioactive decay ($s=0, 2$), magnetar engine, and CSI+RD models, combined with early electron-scattering profile modeling using Monte Carlo radiative transfer and Swift-XRT X-ray analysis.
assumptions: Electron scattering in the unshocked dense CSM dominates the Lorentzian-like wing profile in the earliest optical spectra.
limits: Pure radioactive decay and pure magnetar-driven models fail to match observed multi-color light curves and physical progenitor constraints.

analysis.reason: The paper provides an observational and theoretical analysis of the long-term (~50 yr) evolution of the 35-day super-orbital cycle in the X-ray binary Her X-1, demonstrating that neutron star free precession driven by accretion-induced moment of inertia evolution can serve as the underlying clock for warped accretion disk precession.
analysis.result: The 35-day precessional period exhibits a secular decline with $\dot{P}_{35} \approx (-5.04 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ as measured by RXTE/ASM and MAXI, and piecewise rates of $(-1.3 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ and $(-4.7 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ separated by the anomalous low state (ALS) at MJD 51500, matching the theoretical prediction of accretion-driven moment-of-inertia evolution $\dot{P}_{\rm pr}/P_{\rm pr} \approx -(\dot{\Delta I})/\Delta I \sim -\frac{1}{4}(\dot{M}/M_{\rm NS})(P_{\rm pr}/P_*) \sim -2\times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ yielding $\dot{P}_{\rm pr} \sim -6\times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$.
analysis.reading_entry: 2.1 35-day period evolution using RXTE/ASM - Swift/BAT - MAXI X-ray light curve
analysis.problem: Whether the 35-day super-orbital cycle in Her X-1 is purely governed by chaotic accretion disk precession or paced by a quasi-stable underlying clock mechanism such as neutron star free precession.
analysis.method: Multi-mission X-ray light curve analysis (CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, MAXI) spanning over 50 years using sliding-window phase averaging and parabolic $O-C$ phase fitting: $\phi(t) = \phi_0(T_0) + \frac{P_{35} - P_0}{P_0 P_{35}}(t - T_0) + \frac{\dot{P}_{35}}{2 P_{35}^2}(t - T_0)^2$, combined with a biaxial neutron star free precession model governed by $\frac{\dot{P}_{\mathrm{pr}}}{P_{\mathrm{pr}}}=\frac{\dot{P}_{*}}{P_{*}}+\frac{\dot{I}_{3}}{I_{3}}-\frac{\dot{(\Delta I)}}{\Delta I}+(\tan\theta)\dot{\theta}$.
assumptions: The 35-day X-ray cycle is paced by the free precession of a biaxial neutron star whose oblateness evolves due to steady accretion.
limits: During anomalous low states (ALS), outer disk synchronization with the neutron star precession is temporarily lost, causing discrete period jumps.
citation_leads: 2.1 35-day period evolution using RXTE/ASM - Swift/BAT - MAXI X-ray light curve: “The result is $\dot{P}_{35}\approx(-5.04\pm 0.1)\times 10^{-5}$ s s-1.”
2.2 NS 35-day period evolution: “$\frac{\dot{P}_{\mathrm{pr}}}{P_{\mathrm{pr}}}=\frac{\dot{P}_{*}}{P_{*}}+\frac{\dot{I}_{3}}{I_{3}}-\frac{\dot{(\Delta I)}}{\Delta I}+(\tan\theta)\dot{\theta}\,.$”

3 Discussion and conclusion: “During the ALS the outer parts of the accretion disk is thought to move toward
the orbital plane, the synchronization with the NS free precession period is lost, and the accretion disk precession period becomes uncertain.”
References: “Two ~35 day clocks in Hercules X-1: evidence for neutron star free precession.”
analysis.research_progress: Confirmed secular spin-up of the 35-day precession cycle with $\dot{P}_{35} \sim -10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$, rule out random-walk phase divergence, and showed that residuals bounded by $\Delta \phi \sim \pm 0.1$ are punctuated by crustal stress adjustments with $\Delta P_{\rm pr}/P_{\rm pr} \approx \Delta \theta/\theta \sim \pm 0.03$.

Dashed curves show two parabolic approximations (see formula ( 2 ) and Table 2 ) of turn-ons corresponding to 35-day period decrease rate $\dot{P}_{35}\approx(-1.3\pm 0.2)\times 10^{-5}$ s s -1 and $\approx(-4.7\pm 0.1)\times 10^{-5}$ s s -1 for left (before MJD 51500) and right (after MJD 51500) data (taking into account the phase shift during the ALS discussed in ( Staubert et al., 2009a ) ).

analysis.reason: This work performs an unprecedented multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling (PPM) of the nearest millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 combining HST, NICER, XMM-Newton, and NuSTAR datasets to obtain the tightest neutron star radius and equation of state constraints to date.
analysis.result: Using the ST+PDT+EL+PL surface emission configuration, the headline PPM inference yields an equatorial radius of $R_{\rm eq} = 11.35_{-0.39}^{+0.40}\,\mathrm{km}$ (or $R_{\rm eq} = 11.345_{-0.388}^{+0.399}\,\mathrm{km}$) and a mass of $M = 1.377_{-0.034}^{+0.038}\,M_{\odot}$. The whole-surface warm emission has an effective temperature in the stellar frame of $\log_{10}(T_{\rm else}\,[\mathrm{K}]) = 5.451 \pm 0.008$ ($T_{\rm else} = (2.82 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$), translating to an observer at infinity to $T_{\rm else}^{\infty} = T_{\rm else}/(1+z) = (2.26 \pm 0.03) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$ via the gravitational redshift $1+z = \left(1 - \frac{2GM}{R_{\rm eq}c^2}\right)^{-1/2}$, with observed flux scaling as $F \propto (R_{\rm eq}^{\infty}/d)^2 \sigma (T_{\rm else}^{\infty})^4$. The pulsed non-thermal power-law component exhibits photon index $\Gamma_{\rm PL} = 1.310_{-0.061}^{+0.054}$ and pulsed amplitude $A_{\rm PL} = 0.684_{-0.057}^{+0.059}$. At the 95% credibility level, the upper limit of the neutron star radius is reduced by $\approx 0.4\text{--}0.6\,\mathrm{km}$, yielding inferred radius at $1.4\,M_{\odot}$ of $R_{1.4} = 11.52_{-0.50}^{+0.66}\,\mathrm{km}$ (piecewise polytrope) and $11.48_{-0.52}^{+0.61}\,\mathrm{km}$ (speed of sound), ruling out stiff EOSs with $R > 12.0\,\mathrm{km}$ at 68% credibility.
analysis.problem: Previous radius inferences of PSR J0437-4715 suffered from strong degeneracies between the pulsed non-thermal magnetospheric power-law tail, the soft thermal hot spots, and the diffuse warm stellar surface. Without joint far-UV (HST) and hard X-ray (NuSTAR) coverage, the non-thermal normalization and whole-surface emission were unconstrained, leading to divergent radius posteriors ranging from $\sim 7.9\,\mathrm{km}$ up to $\sim 14.1\,\mathrm{km}$.
analysis.method: The authors perform multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling within an extended X-PSI Bayesian inference framework over $0.007\text{--}16.0\,\mathrm{keV}$, integrating $2.56\,\mathrm{Ms}$ of NICER XTI data, $113\,\mathrm{ks}$ of XMM-Newton EPIC MOS data, $221\,\mathrm{ks}$ of NuSTAR FPM data ($3.0\text{--}16.0\,\mathrm{keV}$), and HST STIS far-UV spectroscopy ($1150\text{--}1700\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$). The likelihood couples a modified Gaussian log-likelihood for HST STIS fluxes $\mathcal{L}(\theta,\mathbf{B})=\sum_{i,k}\left[\frac{(c_{ik}(\theta)-d_{ik}+B_{i}T_{\rm exp}\int_{\phi_{k}}d\phi)^2}{\sigma_{ik}^2}+\ln(2\pi\sigma_{ik}^2)\right]$ with Poisson likelihoods for X-ray timing data. The geometric model combines a northern single-temperature (ST) hydrogen atmosphere spot (NSXH), an equatorial/southern protruding dual-temperature (PDT) spot, an unheated warm surface (EL) with partially ionized hydrogen (NSXHp), and an observer-frame sinusoidally modulated power law $F(E,\phi)=N_{\mathrm{PL}}(E/1\,\mathrm{keV})^{-\Gamma_{\mathrm{PL}}}[1+A_{\mathrm{PL}}\cos(2\pi(\phi-\phi_{\mathrm{PL}}))]$ evaluated using MultiNest nested sampling.
assumptions: The warm unheated stellar surface emits as a partially ionized hydrogen atmosphere (NSXHp) at uniform effective temperature $T_{\rm else}$ over the region outside the hot spots.

analysis.research_progress: By simultaneously resolving the degeneracy between compactness $M/R_{\rm eq}$ (from soft X-ray pulse profiles) and redshifted radiation radius $R_{\rm eq}^{\infty} = R_{\rm eq}\left(1 - \frac{2GM}{R_{\rm eq}c^2}\right)^{-1/2}$ (from FUV flux constraints), this work eliminates the bimodal posterior around $12\,\mathrm{km}$, narrows the radius credible interval to $\pm 0.40\,\mathrm{km}$, and brings PSR J0437-4715 into close agreement with PPM measurements of PSR J0030+0451 and PSR J0614-3329.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the physical conditions required to form micron-sized presolar graphite grains in supernova ejecta, providing key scaling relations linking grain sizes to explosion energy, ejecta mass, progenitor radius, and nickel heating.
analysis.result: In Ni-free ejecta undergoing matter-dominated adiabatic expansion, the final graphite grain radius scales analytically as $r_{\rm gr,final} \simeq 615\,\mu\mathrm{m}\,(E_{\rm exp}/10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg})^{-3/2}\,(M_{\rm ej}/5\,M_\odot)^{5/2}\,(R_0/10^{12}\,\mathrm{cm})^{-2}\,(X'_{\rm C}/3\times 10^{-3})$, governed by the local key parameter combination $X'_{\rm C}\rho_{2000}\tau_{\rm cool,2000} \propto X'_{\rm C}E_{\rm exp}^{-3/2}M_{\rm ej}^{5/2}R_0^{-2}$. Micron-sized grains ($r_{\rm gr} \gtrsim 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$) require low explosion energy ($E_{\rm exp} \lesssim 10^{49}\text{--}10^{50}\,\mathrm{erg}$), massive ejecta, and negligible radioactive $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ heating, as $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ heating delays dust condensation until the ejecta expands to much lower densities, suppressing final grain radii below $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.
analysis.reading_entry: 4.2 Analytical estimates of the grain size
analysis.problem: Presolar graphite grains extracted from meteorites exhibit supernova isotopic signatures and reach sizes $\gtrsim 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, whereas standard core-collapse supernova models ($E_{\rm exp} \sim 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$, $M_{\rm ej} \sim 10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ni} \sim 0.01\text{--}0.1\,M_\odot$) typically predict graphite grain sizes below $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.
analysis.method: A spherical, uniformly expanding one-zone ejecta dynamics model coupled to an energy equation including radioactive $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$ decay heating $\dot{Q}$, $p\,dV$ work, and radiative cooling. Dust formation is calculated using classical homogeneous nucleation theory for carbon monomers and moment equations $dK_j^{(\ell)}/dt$ coupled to key species depletion, with analytical scaling relations derived for the matter-dominated adiabatic limit ($T \propto \rho^{2/3}$) at the reference condensation temperature $T = 2000\,\mathrm{K}$.
assumptions: Constant carbon sticking probability $\alpha_{\rm C} = 1$ and pre-set effective carbon mass fraction $X'_{\rm C}$ assuming molecular CO formation locks up equal parts of carbon and oxygen without solving explicit time-dependent chemical networks.
limits: Calculations do not resolve the multi-dimensional density and composition structure, clumping, or radioactive chemical destruction within real supernova ejecta.
citation_leads: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta: “Presolar graphite grains with supernova isotopic signatures provide direct evidence that large graphite grains formed in supernova ejecta.”
3.1 Overview of nucleation theory: “In cooling and expanding ejecta, atoms and molecules in the gas phase form condensation nuclei, which subsequently grow into dust grains.”

4.2 Analytical estimates of the grain size: “The numerical results thus reveal an approximately single-valued relation between $X^{\prime}_{\rm C}\rho_{2000}\tau_{\rm cool,2000}$ and the final grain size over the explored range of Ni-free adiabatic models.”

4.4 The effect of Ni heating: “Radioactive heating lengthens $\tau_{{\rm cool},2000}$, but it also delays condensation while the ejecta continue to expand, lowering $\rho_{2000}$ by orders of magnitude”
5.3 Caveat: “The present one-zone calculations identify conditions favorable for graphite formation, but do not resolve the density and composition structure, clumping, or mixing within the ejecta.”
Appendix B Effective growth window: “Because the nucleation rate depends exponentially on the supersaturation ratio, this temperature width is much smaller than unity in logarithmic temperature.”
analysis.research_progress: Unifies grain growth physics via the dimensionless collision-to-saturation timescale parameter and maps it directly onto bulk supernova observables, establishing that low-energy ($E_{\rm exp} \ll 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$), $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$-poor core-collapse supernovae are the requisite stellar environment for synthesizing micron-sized presolar graphite grains.

analysis.reason: Investigates the quiescent post-outburst state of the ultrafast nova and intermediate polar candidate V1674 Her with joint NuSTAR and XMM-Newton observations, demonstrating magnetic field survival and constraining WD shock energetics.
analysis.result: The quiescent X-ray spectrum is consistent with multi-temperature shock emission with a high maximum temperature $kT_{\max} \ge 69\text{ keV}$, yielding a massive white dwarf estimate of $M_{\text{WD}} = 1.26_{-0.56}^{+0.11}\,M_\odot$ (or $\approx 1.35\,M_\odot$). Timing analysis yields a spin period $P = 501.31 \pm 0.19\text{ s}$ (and $501.35 \pm 0.19\text{ s}$) with energy-dependent modulation (pulse fraction dropping from $60\%$ to $47\%$) and strict phase alignment of pulse minima between the 2021 outburst and 2024 quiescence.
analysis.reading_entry: IV.4 V1674 Her as a fast magnetic rotator
analysis.problem: Uncovering the origin of the hard X-ray emission (thermal accretion shock vs. Comptonized column), constraining the white dwarf mass, and explaining the rapid optical rise and early $\gamma$-ray emission in the presence of strong magnetic rotation.
analysis.method: Quasi-simultaneous XMM-Newton (0.3–10 keV) and NuSTAR (3–40 keV) spectral modeling using multi-temperature plasma (`mkcflow`), Comptonization (`compTT`), and magnetized post-shock accretion column (`ipolar30kK`) models, combined with Lomb-Scargle and Phase Dispersion Minimization (PDM) timing analyses.
assumptions: The large-scale dipolar magnetic field structure survives the nova thermonuclear runaway and anchors accretion and burning at the magnetic poles.
limits: A severe degeneracy between high shock temperature $kT_{\max}$ and sub-solar metallicity ($Z/Z_\odot < 0.01$) exists due to the lack of detectable iron lines and subtle continuum curvature below $40\text{ keV}$.
citation_leads: III.1 Spectral analysis: “The subtle continuum curvature below 40 keV makes it difficult to unambiguously decouple a very high $kT_{\max}$ from an extremely low metallicity ($Z/Z_{\odot}<0.01$), which is required to suppress the H- and He-like iron lines.”

III.2 Timing analysis: “Despite the transition from a nuclear-burning SSS phase to an accretion-powered quiescent state, the pulse minima show a remarkably small phase shift. This stability indicates that the magnetic poles remained the primary site of both”
V Conclusions: “By folding both the 2021 and 2024 light curves with the same spin ephemeris, we found that the pulse minima are aligned.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that V1674 Her acts as a fast magnetic rotator ($\Omega \ge 0.01\text{ rad s}^{-1}$, $B > 10^5\text{ G}$), providing a viable mechanism where centrifugal magnetic winds collide with early ejecta to power the concurrent optical and $\gamma$-ray peaks.

analysis.result: The authors derive the exact bivariate differential rate distribution (DRD) for velocity kicks in isotropic clusters, yielding closed-form DRD solutions for King models and nuclear star clusters (NSCs) with $\rho \propto r^{-\gamma}$. For extreme-eccentricity orbits ($1-e \ll 1$) in NSCs, strong scatterings at apocenter can impart angular momentum jumps $\Delta J \approx J_c - J$ (where $J_c^5 = \frac{85}{3} \frac{k \sigma(a)^3}{n(a) \langle M_{\rm s}^2 \rangle \ln\Lambda} \frac{G^{7/2} M_\bullet^{9/2} M}{a^{3/2} c^5}$), ejecting compact objects back into the two-body relaxation regime and canceling EMRIs with a scale-invariant rate $N_{\rm CE} \sim \Gamma_{{\rm CE},o} t_{\rm GW} \propto a^0$. The orbit-averaged stellar ejection rate near pericenter scales as $\langle \Gamma_{\rm ej} \rangle \approx \frac{16\pi}{5 P (\gamma-1)} \frac{M_{\rm s}}{M_\bullet^2} r_{\rm inf}^\gamma \rho_{\rm inf} a^{3-\gamma} (1-e)^{1-\gamma}$.
analysis.problem: Standard cluster evolution and loss-cone dynamics rely on low-order diffusion coefficients from weak small-angle scatterings, which fail to capture rare, non-diffusive phase-space jumps caused by strong gravitational scatterings that can eject stars or disrupt extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs).
analysis.method: Analytical formulation of hyperbolic encounters in spherical isotropic star clusters by projecting velocity kicks into parallel and perpendicular components ($\Delta v_{||}, \Delta v_\perp$), transforming the kick distribution into a two-dimensional planar slice integral over field star distribution functions $f(v_f)$: $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2\Gamma}{\mathrm{d}\Delta v_{||} \mathrm{d}\Delta v_{\perp} } = 8\pi G^2 M_{\rm s}^2 \frac{\Delta v_{\perp}}{(\Delta v_{||}^2 + \Delta v_{\perp}^2)^{5/2}} \int_{\Delta \hat{v}\cdot \vec{v}_f = \kappa} f(v_f)\, \mathrm{d}A$, mapping to action space $(E, J)$ via pericenter radial approximation, and orbit-averaging scattering rates.
citation_leads: Action Space and Astrophysical Applications: “In this standard picture, EMRIs totally decouple from stellar perturbations once $t_\mathrm{GW} \ll t_\mathrm{AM}$. However, one can hypothesize that although AM diffusion appears to be subdominant, there is still a rare chance of a close”
Action Space and Astrophysical Applications: “To express the previously derived rate distribution in terms of the specific energy and AM, it would be ideal to use the Jacobian of the map”

Action Space and Astrophysical Applications: “If energy relaxation happens at or faster than the orbital timescale, strong kicks that might have led to an ejection in isolation can ultimately be swamped by the rapid diffusion from weak encounters, leading to potentially enhanced loss”

figures.caption: Figure 6: Accumulated numbers of EMRI cancellations, $N_{\rm CE}$, in the space of semimajor axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$, within the GW-dominated zone (i.e. where $t_{\rm GW}<t_{\rm AM}$). $M_{\bullet}$, $M$, and $M_{\rm s}$ are fixed at $10^{6}$, $10$, and $1\,M_{\odot}$, respectively. The top panel shows $\gamma=3/2$, the middle displays the Bahcall-Wolf solution of $\gamma=7/4$, and the bottom panel shows $\gamma=2$. The magenta contour in each plot displays where $N_{\mathrm{CE}}=1$. We exclude points where $J_{c}-J<5\sqrt{\langle\Delta J^{2}\rangle_{o}P}$. We see that for all $\gamma$ values, the $N_{\rm CE}$ contour lies below the $t_{\rm GW}=t_{\rm AM}$ contour, indicating that EMRI cancellation will suppress the low-eccentricity tail of observed EMRI distributions.
figures.label: Fig. 6
figures.physical_core: Maps the accumulated number of EMRI cancellations, $N_{\rm CE}$, across semimajor axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$ in the GW-dominated zone, where $t_{\rm GW}<t_{\rm AM}$. figures.caption: Figure 8: Plots showing different ejection regimes in the space of semimajor axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$, for black hole masses of $10^{6}\,M_{\odot}$ (top panel), $10^{5}\,M_{\odot}$ (middle panel), and $10^{4}\,M_{\odot}$ (bottom panel). All systems take $M=M_{\rm s}=1\,M_{\odot}$. Solid lines show $\Delta E_{c,\max}=E$ for different values of $\gamma$ (color-coded as per the inset key). Regions to the left of these solid lines are in the saturated kick regime. The dashed lines indicate where $t_{E}=P$ for each system of the same color; regions left of these are in the diffusively saturated kick regime. Saturation of ejections via strong scatterings becomes important for small $M_{\bullet}$, large $a$, and large $\gamma$. The hatched region is where $r_{p}\leq 8R_{g}$, with $R_{g}=GM_{\bullet}/c^{2}$, a typical minimum pericenter to avoid a plunge. The dotted line notates the $r_{\mathrm{inf}}$ corresponding to $\gamma=7/4$.
figures.label: Fig. 8
figures.physical_core: Shows ejection regimes in $(a,e)$ for three central black-hole masses. The curves mark $\u0394 E_{c,\max}=E$ and $t_E=P$; the regions to their left identify saturated and diffusively saturated kick regimes, respectively. The figure illustrates that saturation of strong-scattering ejections becomes important for smaller $M_{\bullet}$, larger $a$, and larger $\gamma$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first systematic study of black hole spin evolution across the continuous transition from weakly magnetized (SANE) to magnetically arrested disks (MAD) using 3D GRMHD simulations with live spacetime updates, providing an analytical subgrid prescription for spin-up/spin-down equilibria in relativistic jets and compact accretors.
analysis.result: The equilibrium spin declines steeply with normalized horizon magnetic flux $\tilde{\phi} \equiv \phi / \phi_{\rm MAD}$, dropping from $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows ($\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 0.2$), through $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}(\tilde{\phi}=0.5) \approx 0.5$, down to $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.05\text{--}0.06$ at MAD saturation ($\tilde{\phi} = 1$). In the sustained MAD regime, the BH reaches within $3\%\text{--}6\%$ of its equilibrium spin by accreting only $\lesssim 50\%$ of its initial mass.
analysis.reading_entry: II Black hole spin evolution in a nutshell
analysis.problem: Prior GRMHD simulations assumed static black hole spacetimes and explored only binary extremes (pure SANE or saturated MAD), lacking continuous quantitative descriptions of BH spin evolution and equilibrium spins across intermediate magnetic flux levels.
analysis.method: Performed long-duration 3D GRMHD simulations with the H-AMR code tracking horizon energy and angular momentum fluxes ($dM_{\rm BH}/dt = \int T^r_t dA_{\theta\varphi}$, $dJ/dt = -\int T^r_\varphi dA_{\theta\varphi}$), updating the Kerr-Schild metric self-consistently with a moving boundary at $r_{\rm b} = 0.7 r_{\rm H}$. Numerical fits for hydrodynamical and electromagnetic fluxes yield the spin rate $s = l_{\rm HD} + l_{\rm EM} - 2a_\star(e_{\rm HD} + e_{\rm EM})$.
assumptions: Coordinate metric changes instantaneously over time steps without backreacting on external gas through non-local metric work terms ($|E_{\rm miss}| / \Delta M_{\rm BH} \lesssim 2\%\text{--}4\%$)
limits: Fitting formulae calibrated for $\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 1.2$ in radiatively inefficient thick disks; radiative cooling (e.g., in collapsars or thin disks) shifts $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}$ higher
citation_leads: Black Hole Spin Evolution in Magnetized Accretion Flows: “The equilibrium spin falls steeply with flux, from $a_{\rm\star;eq}\approx 0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows through $a_{\rm\star;eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}=0.5)\approx 0.5$ to $a_{\rm\star;eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}=1)\approx 0.06$ in sustained”
II.2 Final spin: “In the MAD regime, $\tilde{\phi}\gtrsim 1$, the BH needs to accrete $\lesssim 50\%$ of its initial mass to come within $3$–$6\%$ of $a_{\star;\rm eq}$, for all three initial spins”

IV.2.1 Time evolution of the BHs: “The high-$\dot{M}_{0}$ MAD models with $a_{\rm\star,0}=0.1$ and $0.5$ both spin down and level off at an equilibrium spin $a_{\star;\rm eq}\approx 0.05$–$0.06$, between the estimates for radiatively inefficient MADs”

IV.2.2 Black hole spin evolution: “We use our simulations to construct a prescription for BH spin evolution across the range of horizon magnetic fluxes, $\tilde{\phi}\lesssim 1.2$, connecting the SANE and MAD limits.”

V.1.3 X-ray binaries: “If the jets are weak, $\tilde{\phi}\lesssim 0.2$, the BH spins up at nearly the thin-disk rate toward $a_{\rm\star}\gtrsim 0.9$, so thin-disk prescriptions remain a good approximation. Only powerful jets, $\tilde{\phi}\gtrsim 0.7$,”

Appendix C Work done by the time-dependent metric: “In the massive tori, $M_{\rm torus}/M_{\rm BH,0}\approx 4$–$6$, the omitted work amounts to $\approx 2$–$4\%$ of the total mass-energy growth of the BH, $\Delta M_{\rm BH}$, by the end of the simulations.”
analysis.research_progress: Constructed a unified, continuous prescription connecting SANE and MAD regimes that determines the BH spin evolution rate $da_\star/dt = s(a_\star, \tilde{\phi}) \dot{M}_0 / M_{\rm BH}$ and identified rapid spin-down by powerful jets ($\tilde{\phi} \gtrsim 0.7$) as a mechanism explaining low spin populations in binary black hole mergers.

analysis.reason: The study focuses on Galactic long-period Mira variables and infrared spectroscopic classification of an evolved Super-AGB star candidate, which pertains to late-stage stellar evolution rather than high-energy transient physics, supernova central engines, or compact object observational signatures.
analysis.result: Among 13 Galactic very long period ($P \gtrsim 1000\ \mathrm{d}$) Mira variables, 12 are massive O-rich AGB stars, while IRAS 19552+3142 is identified as the longest-period ($P \approx 1060\ \mathrm{d}$) C-rich AGB star in the Milky Way. Spectral energy distribution modeling indicates a bolometric luminosity of $L_{1-30\,\mu\mathrm{m}} \approx (1-4) \times 10^4\ L_\odot$, radius $R_* \approx 500-1000\ R_\odot$, and a high dust-driven mass-loss rate: $$\dot{M} \approx 10^{-4}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}(\tau_{10})\left(\frac{550\,\mathrm{cm^2\,g^{-1}}}{\kappa_{10}}\right)\left(\frac{R_{\rm in}}{1.5\times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}}\right)\left(\frac{v_d}{15\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}}\right)\left(\frac{10^{-3}}{r_{\rm dg}}\right)$$, consistent with a thermally pulsing Super-AGB (TP-SAGB) star in the hot bottom burning turn-off phase.
analysis.problem: Identifying true extremely long-period ($P > 1000\ \mathrm{d}$) Mira variables in the Galactic plane to study massive AGB/SAGB stars is impeded by interstellar and circumstellar extinction, severe saturation, and alias period errors in low-cadence mid-infrared surveys.
analysis.method: Combined high-cadence ($1-3\ \mathrm{d}$) Palomar Gattini-IR (PGIR) $J$-band time-series photometry with Gaussian Process regression to extract fundamental pulsation periods, and conducted near-infrared spectroscopy ($0.7-2.5\ \mu\mathrm{m}$, $R \approx 2000$) using IRTF/SpeX in SXD mode to detect molecular absorption bands ($\mathrm{TiO}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{CO}$, $\mathrm{C_2}$).

analysis.reason: The paper develops a rigorous characteristic-function formalism to construct tractable likelihoods and optimal sufficient statistics for non-Gaussian stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds produced by compact binary coalescences (BBH/BNS/NSBH). It directly informs searches for intermittent and popcorn-type compact object merger backgrounds relevant to high-energy transient source populations.
analysis.result: The exact non-Gaussian GWB likelihood is decoupled via Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation into the characteristic function of single mergers $z(\eta;\Lambda)$. For a toy model with segment noise $\sigma^2$, event rate $\bar{N}$, and amplitude variance $A_0^2$, the exact detection floor flattens at $\bar{N} A_0^2 \simeq 10^{-2}$ for $\bar{N} \gtrsim 10^{-2}$ and drops by a factor of $\sim 3$ toward $\bar{N} = 10^{-3}$. The single-component likelihood $\mathcal{L}_{M=1}$ is sensitive only to the degenerate combination $\bar{N} A_0^2$, whereas multi-component Gaussian mixtures $\mathcal{L}_M$ converge to the exact detection threshold with only 3 components.
analysis.reading_entry: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background
analysis.problem: Stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds from stellar-mass compact binaries are fundamentally non-Gaussian due to finite merger rates, but standard isotropic/Gaussian searches using only the cross-correlation statistic lose sensitivity to intermittent, high-amplitude events and suffer from severe parameter degeneracies.
analysis.method:
The framework linearizes the signal within the Whittle likelihood exponent using an auxiliary variable $\eta_{I
u}$, mapping the Poisson-marginalized likelihood to an integral over the single-event characteristic function $z(\eta;\Lambda) \equiv \langle \exp[-i\mathrm{Re}\sum_{I,
u}\eta_{I
u}^* h_{I
u}(\lambda)] angle_\pi$. Tractable likelihood families are constructed via basis-function expansions $ ar{N}(z(\eta;\Lambda)-1) \simeq \sum_n w_n \psi_n(\eta)$, evaluating event-count truncation $\mathcal{L}_{K \leq n}$, Gaussian mixtures $\mathcal{L}_M$ with basis $\psi_n(\eta) = \exp [ -  rac{1}{2} C_n (\eta_1 + \eta_2)^2 ]$, and Taylor expansions $\mathcal{L}_{2m}$ with $\psi_n(\eta) = (\eta_1 + \eta_2)^{2n}$.
assumptions: Merger events occur as a temporal Poisson process with mean number of events $\bar{N}$ per data segment.
limits: Truncation of event counts $\mathcal{L}_{K \leq n}$ leads to parameter recovery biases at high merger rates $\bar{N}$.
citation_leads: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background: “The stochastic gravitational-wave background from stellar-mass compact binaries is non-Gaussian since it is made up of a finite number of individual mergers.”

Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background: “Choosing the most efficient statistics is then the same problem as approximating the characteristic function with the fewest terms.”

II.B. Gaussian mixture approximation: “The component of scale $C _ { n }$ corresponds to segments whose signal power is of that order. Thus, the constant component corresponds to segments with no events, while the largest scale corresponds to segments with several events.”

IV. Results: “The posterior from the single-component likelihood $\mathcal { L } _ { M = 1 }$ is informative only on the degenerate combination ${ \bar { N } } A _ { 0 } ^ { 2 } .$ and its detection floor is above that of the exact likelihood.”
analysis.research_progress: Unifies intermittent popcorn background searches and standard cross-correlation methods into a generalized characteristic-function likelihood framework, demonstrating that higher-order statistics derived from basis expansions break the $\bar{N}-A_0^2$ degeneracy and lower detection thresholds.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Detection and recovery for the event-count family of ( 39 ), for a Gaussian intermittent signal in two co-located and co-aligned detectors. The top-left panel is the smallest detectable cross power $\bar{N}A_{0}^{2}$ versus the rate $\bar{N}$ for $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 1}$, $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 2}$, $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 3}$ and the exact mixture; this is the detection floor of each likelihood. The callouts give, at the three marked rates, the maximum-likelihood recovery of $(\log_{10}\bar{N},\log_{10}A_{0}^{2})$. Each thin curve is the $\Delta\ln\mathcal{L}=-3$ contour of one realization, and the cyan cross marks the true parameter values. Where the background is rare and loud, the one-event truncation already reaches the exact detection floor and centers on the true parameter values, while at higher rates the low truncations stay on the exact floor and bias the estimate. The family closes in on the exact mixture as more event counts are kept.

analysis.reason: The paper introduces SuperCrude, a fully analytic, physically motivated equation of state (EoS) designed for explosive astrophysical hydrodynamics (e.g. supernovae and compact object flows). It circumvents the table-boundary and GPU porting bottlenecks of tabulated EoS like helmeos, achieving competitive hydrodynamical accuracy and >3x speedup.
analysis.result: SuperCrude models the fluid via decomposed components $P = P_{\mathrm{deg}} + P_{\mathrm{gas}} + P_{\mathrm{rad}} + P_{\mathrm{pairs}}$ and $\mathcal{E} = \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{deg}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{gas}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{rad}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pairs}}$, recovering sound speed $c_s = \sqrt{(B_{\mathrm{deg}} + B_{\mathrm{Th}})/(\rho h)}$ with relativistic enthalpy $h = 1 + (P + \mathcal{E})/(\rho c^2)$. In hydrodynamic closures $P(\rho, \mathcal{E})$, errors are $<5\%$ (mostly $<10^{-3}$) relative to helmeos; the peak error in $\Gamma_H \equiv 1 + P/\mathcal{E}$ is $1.3\% - 2.5\%$ and $\Gamma_1$ error is $\lesssim 5\%$. In 1D hydro tests, density $L_1$ error is $3.64 \times 10^{-3}$, and single-zone execution time decreases from $571\,\mathrm{ns}$ (helmeos) to $89.7\,\mathrm{ns}$.
analysis.problem: Standard astrophysical EoS codes (such as the tabular helmeos) rely on high-order table interpolation, which suffers from out-of-boundary failures, poor vectorization/memory bottlenecks on GPUs, and high computational overhead for explosive fluid dynamics where hydro closure primarily needs $P(\rho, \mathcal{E})$ rather than highly resolved temperature.
analysis.method: Formulated a unified analytic Helmholtz free energy density $\mathcal{F}(\rho, T)$ combining zero-temperature degenerate electron gas with smooth finite-temperature Fermi gas corrections ($k T_0 \equiv (6/\pi^2)\epsilon_*$), radiation ($P_{\mathrm{rad}} = a T^4 / 3$), and an analytic pair-production suppression factor $P_{\mathrm{pairs}} \approx \frac{1}{3} a T^4 \times \frac{7}{4} e^{-(T_p/T)^{n_p}}$ ($k T_p = 0.386\,m_e c^2, n_p = 1.552$). Evaluated thermodynamic consistency, sound speed $\Gamma_1 = (\partial \ln P / \partial \ln \rho)_s$, temperature inversion via a Newton-Raphson scheme, and 1D/double-detonation hydrodynamic benchmarks.

analysis.reason: This paper establishes a novel method combining FRB dispersion measures with X-ray absorption columns to determine the metallicity of the Milky Way circumgalactic medium. It directly impacts the estimation of the Galactic foreground DM and the study of the diffuse halo baryon reservoir.
analysis.result: Using 25 localized FRB sightlines at $z < 0.3$, the bootstrap median metallicity of the Milky Way CGM is inferred to be $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.12_{-0.04}^{+0.09} \, Z_{\odot}$ for diffuse baryon fraction $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.0$, $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.26_{-0.12}^{+0.18} \, Z_{\odot}$ for $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.6$, and $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.39_{-0.20}^{+0.26} \, Z_{\odot}$ for $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$. Even at the conservative limit $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.0$, the halo metallicity exceeds pristine IGM accretion ($Z_{\mathrm{IGM}} \lesssim 0.1 \, Z_{\odot}$), whereas $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$ produces unphysical super-solar metallicities ($Z \gg 1 \, Z_{\odot}$) along multiple sightlines.
analysis.problem: Converting soft X-ray metal absorption columns (such as $\mathrm{O\,VII}$ and $\mathrm{O\,VIII}$) into total CGM gas mass suffers from an inherent degeneracy with assumed halo metallicity, leaving the true chemical enrichment and baryon content of the hot volume-filling CGM unconstrained.
analysis.method: The framework compares metallicity-dependent X-ray absorption DMs (referenced to $Z_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0.3 \, Z_{\odot}$ under collisional ionization equilibrium) to metallicity-independent FRB DMs via $Z_{\mathrm{MW,CGM}} = Z_{\mathrm{ref}} \left[ \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{metal}, Z_{\mathrm{ref}}} / \left(\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{obs}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW, ISM}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{host}}/(1+z)\right) \right]$. Host galaxy DM contributions are sampled via Monte Carlo from a log-normal distribution with $e^{\mu_{\mathrm{host}}} = 100$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{host}} = 1.0$, rejecting non-physical realizations with $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW,CGM}} \le 0$ until $10^5$ valid draws are acquired.
assumptions: The hot phase of the CGM ($T \gtrsim 10^6 \, \mathrm{K}$) is under collisional ionization equilibrium (CIE) with ionization fractions determined from O VIII to O VII ratios or upper limits.
limits: Subtracting the mean cosmic Macquart relation systematically over-corrects low-redshift sightlines ($z < 0.3$), which have fewer intervening halos, causing an over-subtraction of $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}}$ and artificially high metallicities at $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$.

analysis.reason: This work directly addresses the physical mechanism of magnetic flux generation, transport, and relativistic jet launching in black hole accretion systems across varying disk thicknesses ($h/r=0.1$--$0.3$) using 3D GRMHD simulations, providing crucial scaling relations for MAD formation timescales and jet power relevant to GRBs, TDEs, and high-energy transients.
analysis.result: Thick disks ($h/r \sim 0.3$) achieve the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state ($\phi_{\rm BH} = 50$) by $t \simeq 2\times 10^4\,r_g/c$ with electromagnetic jet efficiency $\eta_{\rm EM} \ge 100\%$, whereas thinner disks fail to reach MAD within comparable runtimes, giving $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 5$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.1$) for $h/r=0.2$ and $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 3\times 10^{-2}$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.01$) for $h/r=0.1$. The poloidal magnetic pressure ratio and turbulent parameter scale as $\beta_p^{-1} \propto (h/r)^{4.5}$ and $\alpha_\nu \propto (h/r)^{2.5}$, yielding steep transport scalings $v_{\Phi}/V_k \propto v_{\rm acc}/V_k \propto (h/r)^{3.5}$. The required timescale to accumulate MAD-level flux grows dramatically as $t_{\rm MAD} \sim \hat{v}^{-1}(\phi_{\rm MAD}/a_\phi)^{3/(2\xi)}$, taking $t_{\rm MAD} \sim 4\times 10^4\,r_g/c$ for $h/r=0.3$, $\sim 7\times 10^5\,r_g/c$ for $h/r=0.2$, and $\sim 10^8\,r_g/c$ (requiring a minimum flux reservoir radius $r_{\rm MAD}^{\rm min} \sim 1200\,r_g$) for $h/r=0.1$.
analysis.reading_entry: 6 Connection to jet launching and MAD formation
analysis.problem: Whether geometrically thin and moderately thin accretion disks can self-consistently generate large-scale poloidal magnetic flux from purely toroidal magnetic fields via dynamo processes, efficiently transport it inward to the event horizon, and launch powerful relativistic jets.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional ideal GRMHD simulations executed with the H-AMR code in Kerr-Schild coordinates around high-spin black holes ($a = 0.9$ or $0.9375$), initialized with a purely toroidal magnetic field ($\beta_{\rm ini} = 5$) and cooled via Noble et al. prescriptions to maintain disk aspect ratios $h/r = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$. Analyses employ azimuthal Reynolds decomposition $X = \langle X \rangle + \delta X$ with mean-field induction $\partial_t \langle\mathbf{B}\rangle = \boldsymbol{\nabla} \times (\langle\mathbf{u}\rangle \times \langle\mathbf{B}\rangle + \boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}})$, Fourier modal decomposition of the turbulent EMF $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}} = \langle\delta\mathbf{u} \times \delta\mathbf{B}\rangle$, and magnetic flux advection tracing $v_\Phi = -\partial_t \Phi / \partial_r \Phi$.
assumptions: Initial magnetic field is strictly toroidal with uniform plasma $\beta=5$, containing zero net initial poloidal magnetic flux.
limits: Finite grid resolution in the thinnest disk ($h/r=0.1$) where the strict linear vertical MRI quality factor $Q_\theta^{\rm Jann}$ drops below recommended thresholds ($Q_\theta^{\rm Jann} < 2$) at $r \lesssim 30\,r_g$.

Analytic flux advection trajectories break down near the innermost stable circular orbit and horizon ($r \lesssim 5\,r_g$), and turbulent reconnection of magnetic loops at large radii may erode the available flux reservoir.
citation_leads: Thinner Disks Struggle to Launch Jets: GRMHD Simulations of Magnetic Field Generation and Transport: “We investigate this connection using three-dimensional GRMHD simulations of disks with $h/r=0.1$–$0.3$, initialized with a toroidal magnetic field with plasma $\beta=5$.”

1 Introduction: “We find that the strength of MRI-driven turbulence depends strongly on the disk thickness, rather than simply on the initial toroidal field strength. The magnetic flux accumulated on the black hole also decreases steeply with decreasing”

3.1 Flux on the black hole: “The thick disk ($h/r\sim 0.3$) reaches the MAD state, conventionally defined by $\phi_{\rm BH}=50$, by $t=2\times 10^{4}\,r_{g}/c$. In contrast, the thinner disks do not approach this state during the duration of our simulations”

3.3 Local turbulent behavior: “In all simulations, we observe an exponential growth of both the turbulent magnetic field, $\delta\beta^{-1}$, and the mean large-scale poloidal field, $\beta_{p}^{-1}$. This growth occurs rapidly, within $\sim 10\Omega_{k}^{-1}$”
4.2 Poloidal magnetic field budget: “Applying Parseval’s theorem, the turbulent EMF can be decomposed into contributions from individual azimuthal modes,”

5.1 Angular momentum transport: “As the disk becomes thinner, the accretion velocity decreases dramatically, from $4\times 10^{-2}V_{k}$ for $h/r\sim 0.3$, to $4.4\times 10^{-3}V_{k}$ for $h/r=0.2$, and finally to $4.5\times 10^{-4}V_{k}$ for $h/r=0.1$.”

5.2 Large scale magnetic field transport: “To understand why the magnetic flux accumulates onto the black hole at such different rates, we must examine how magnetic flux is transported through the accretion disk.”

7.1 Conclusion: “Using the measured flux distribution and transport velocities, we estimate the timescale required to accumulate MAD-level magnetic flux. This timescale increases rapidly toward smaller $h/r$, reaching $\sim 10^{8}\,r_{g}/c$ for $h/r=0.1$.”

7.3 Observational consequences: “Even if delayed flux accumulation eventually produces a MAD, the accretion rate may have declined by orders of magnitude, resulting in a much weaker jet despite its high efficiency.”

Appendix B Resolution requirements: “In particular, the characteristic transition wavelengths $\lambda_{I}$ and $\lambda_{S}$, which separate the large-, intermediate-, and small-scale contributions to the dynamo, are nearly identical between simulations”
analysis.research_progress: Reveals that as $h/r$ decreases, the MRI dynamo transitions from a global coherent dynamo to a vertically stratified dynamo confined to the disk surface atmosphere ($2h \lesssim |z| \lesssim 5h$), steepening the accretion velocity to $v_{\rm acc} \propto (h/r)^{3.5}$ (much steeper than standard Shakura-Sunyaev $v_{\rm acc} \propto (h/r)^2$), and causing the timescale to accumulate MAD-level flux to escalate to $\sim 10^8\,r_g/c$ for $h/r=0.1$, which naturally explains delayed or suppressed jet launching in thin-disk transients.

Columns show $t=10^{3}$, $4\times 10^{3}$, and $3.7\times 10^{4}\,r_{g}/c$, while rows correspond to $h/r\sim 0.3$, $0.2$, and $0.1$. The magnetic field becomes more organized with time, with the degree of large-scale coherence decreasing strongly toward thinner disks.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: The time evolution of the azimuthally averaged magnetic field shows that large-scale field coherence decreases as disk thickness falls from $h/r\sim0.3$ to $0.1$.

figures.caption: Figure 14: Spacetime evolution of the signed magnetic flux, $\Phi(r,t)$, for $h/r=0.3$ (a), $0.2$ (b), and $0.1$ (c). Colours indicate magnetic polarity and contours trace magnetic flux surfaces as they evolve through the disk. analysis.reason: This work quantitatively constrains the saturation amplitude and radial magnetic field regeneration of the Tayler instability (TI) in rapidly rotating stars, demonstrating that the Tayler-Spruit dynamo alone is inefficient for angular momentum transport, which directly informs core-collapse progenitor spin, proto-neutron star evolution, and neutron star merger remnant lifetimes.
analysis.result: The Tayler instability in rotating stars ($2\Omega > \omega_{\rm A}$) saturates differently depending on the diffusive excitation mode: magnetostrophic waves (MW, mediated by thermal or viscous diffusion $k_\kappa, k_\nu$) saturate at large magnetic amplitudes $\delta B/B_0 \sim 1$ with radial velocity $\delta u/v_{\rm A} \propto (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-1}$ and regenerate an axisymmetric radial field $\overline{B}_r/B_0 \sim (k_{\rm TI} R)^{-1}$, whereas inertial waves (IW, mediated by magnetic diffusion $k_\eta$) undergo secondary parametric instabilities saturating at much weaker amplitudes $\delta B/B_0 \propto (k_\eta R)^{-1} (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-2} \ll 1$ and $\delta u/v_{\rm A} \propto (k_\eta R)^{-1} (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-1}$.
analysis.reading_entry: IV Nonlinear saturation of the rotating TI
analysis.problem: Resolving whether the nonlinearly saturated Tayler instability in rotating stellar radiative zones saturates at large displacement amplitudes (Fuller et al. 2019 model) or small amplitudes (Spruit 2002 / Zahn et al. 2007), and determining the scaling of regenerated radial magnetic field $\overline{B}_r$ and angular momentum transport.
analysis.method: Direct numerical simulations of 3D incompressible MHD equations under the Boussinesq approximation using the Dedalus pseudo-spectral solver on a spherical domain of radius $R$ with uniform rotation $\boldsymbol{\Omega} = \Omega \hat{z}$ and a background toroidal field $\boldsymbol{B}_0 = B_0 (r/R)\sin\theta\cos\theta\hat{\phi}$ (Alfven frequency $\omega_{\rm A} = B_0/(\sqrt{4\pi\rho}R)$), isolating $k_\kappa$, $k_\nu$, and $k_\eta$ diffusive modes.

analysis.result: Both GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A display an initial $\approx 10\ \mathrm{ms}$ spike with sub-millisecond variability (narrowest features have $\mathrm{FWHM} \approx 90\ \mu\mathrm{s}$ and $\approx 65\ \mu\mathrm{s}$). GRB 910711 exhibits an extremely hard spectrum best fitted by a blackbody ($kT = 216.27^{+43.14}_{-37.21}\ \mathrm{keV}$, $\mathrm{BIC}=39.37$) or a cutoff power law with low-energy photon index $\alpha = 0.87^{+0.68}_{-0.69}$ and peak energy $E_{\rm p} = 957.19^{+508.35}_{-209.02}\ \mathrm{keV}$.
